title: Narrative is the recurrent locus of pipeline drift — protect the company-first story there
description: Across multiple experiments the Narrative stage most often is the first visible point where a company-first Idea is reframed into a product- or orchestration-first story or where unsupported audience/validation claims appear. A focused editorial effort at Narrative (holding upstream inputs constant) is the strongest leverage point for preserving the intended company-first hierarchy.
audience: Prompt engineers, content pipeline owners, product/content leads running Nuëyon.Compose experiments
rationale: The report explicitly finds that Narrative is the most recurrent first visible hierarchy shift (cites across Experiments 007–009). Focusing editorial controls and a test there maps directly to the observed failure mode and to the stated editorial purpose (create a company-first introduction). Gaps/uncertainties: causation is not proven — Idea and Synthesis also produce first-stage drift in some runs (Experiment 008 and 007 run 003). Any trial should therefore preserve inputs to Synthesis/Idea while varying Narrative to isolate effects.
evidence: Facts: “Narrative is the most recurrent first visible hierarchy shift in the available records.” (Cross-experiment patterns). Specific run evidence: Narrative is first in 007 runs 001–002, 008 A-002, and 009 baseline 002/003 and candidates 001–003. Method note: “For each run, ‘first drift’ means the earliest observable stage that departs from the requested company-first editorial hierarchy….” Interpretation: These repeated localizations support the claim that Narrative is the highest-leverage place to test fixes, but the source warns Narrative is not the sole root cause.
